applies_to: any pair carrying text at normal size
space: WCAG relative luminance from linear sRGB
verdict_if_failed: fail; the palette cannot carry body copy on that pair
what_it_does_not_establish: Readability. Contrast ignores font weight, size beyond the two bands, polarity, glare and the spatial frequency of the typeface

applies_to: text at 18.66px bold or 24px regular and above
space: WCAG relative luminance from linear sRGB
what_it_does_not_establish: That the type is actually set at that size in the layout; the gate trusts the claim made in the brief

applies_to: icons, input borders, chart strokes, focus rings
space: WCAG relative luminance from linear sRGB
verdict_if_failed: fail; the boundary is not reliably visible
source: W3C WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.11 Non-text Contrast, AA
what_it_does_not_establish: Whether the element is decorative, which is exempt. That judgement is the designer's and the gate cannot make it

applies_to: any pair the caller declares as carrying meaning by colour alone
formula: simulate protanopia and deuteranopia at severity 1.0, then measure OKLab distance
space: Machado matrices applied in linear sRGB, distance in OKLab
verdict_if_failed: fail on a declared pair; review on any other. SC 1.4.1 is broken by a use and not by a palette, so a collapse on an undeclared pair is reported with the arithmetic rather than judged. Declare pairs with --carries-meaning ROLE+ROLE
source: W3C WCAG 2.2 SC 1.4.1 Use of Color is the requirement; the simulation is Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes 2009, IEEE TVCG; the 0.09 collapse distance is ours
what_it_does_not_establish: Anything about an individual's vision. The matrices model average dichromacy at full severity, not the 8 percent of men who each differ

applies_to: pairs whose hues sit within 30.0 degrees and where both colours carry at least 0.03 chroma, because a near-neutral has no hue to be the same as
threshold: abs(L1 - L2) >= 0.12 passes; below 0.1 fails; between the two is returned for review
formula: abs(OKLCH_L1 - OKLCH_L2), gated on min(C1, C2) >= 0.03
verdict_if_failed: fail below the lower bound; the two read as one colour printed unevenly
source: No published threshold exists. An independent derivation reached the same rule in the same space at 0.1; we hold 0.12, and treat the span between two invented numbers as the range over which nobody knows rather than failing a pair by 0.0004. The 0.03 chroma floor is the one number here that was measured: sweeping the sRGB cube shows a neutral's hue angle swinging by a median 72.7 degrees under a single 8-bit step, more than twice the whole window
what_it_does_not_establish: That 0.12 is a perceptual boundary. It is not. Smaller separations work on large flat areas and fail on a 2px rule

applies_to: any adjacent pair of saturated colours at similar lightness
threshold: not (abs(L1-L2) <= 0.1 and min(C1,C2) >= 0.14 and hue gap >= 100.0)
formula: all three conditions true at once flags the pair
verdict_if_failed: fail; separate the lightness or take chroma off one side
source: The effect is documented, the onset is not. No measured OKLCH threshold exists for chromostereopsis across displays and observers, so this is a screening rule
what_it_does_not_establish: That the edge will vibrate, or that an unflagged edge will not. Display primaries, edge width and adaptation all move the effect

threshold: at most 1 colour at or above C 0.19
verdict_if_failed: fail; one colour leads and the rest support, or nothing leads
source: A composition convention, not a measurement. Held because a palette with two shouting colours has no focal point, which is a hierarchy failure not a colour one. 244 professional photographs were measured against it in references/reference-reading.md and none broke it, but only 7 of them reach C 0.19 anywhere, so the grade stays house-rule: a sample that never approaches a limit cannot confirm it
what_it_does_not_establish: Whether the loud colour is the right one, or whether the category already owns it. Nor whether two loud colours would actually fail, because nothing in the measured set attempts it

applies_to: the palette measured against a representative layout
threshold: combined share of colours at C >= 0.19 is <= 20 percent of the visible area
space: OKLCH, with shares supplied by the layout
verdict_if_failed: fail; the loud colour has become the background
source: Adopted after an independent derivation pointed out that a count cannot tell a 20px accent from a full-bleed panel at the same chroma. Only checked when shares are supplied, because a share nobody measured would be an invented input. The 244-frame set in references/reference-reading.md clears 20 percent in 243 of them with a median share of zero, so on photographic output the threshold is a formality; 3 percent is the line that would bite there and it is deliberately not applied here, because a full-bleed brand panel is not a photograph
what_it_does_not_establish: Anything at all when shares are not supplied. The gate reports skipped rather than passed in that case. It also says nothing useful about a photograph, which reaches this chroma so rarely that a pass carries no information

applies_to: a brand colour placed on the same surface as a photograph of the subject, measured by scripts/sample_reference.py --image REF --check ROLE=HEX
threshold: accent chroma / reference peak chroma <= 1.0 passes; above 1.1 fails; between the two is returned for review
formula: max chroma over the sampled pixels of the reference, against the accent's own chroma
verdict_if_failed: fail; ACCENT-OUTSHOUTS-SUBJECT. The eye lands on the navigation furniture instead of on the thing being sold
source: The rule is a hierarchy convention: in an image whose job is to sell the subject, brand furniture may not be the most saturated thing in the frame. The edge was measured rather than invented, because a maximum is the least stable statistic there is. Across the three food references in this repository at sampling strides 1, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 12 the peak chroma moved by 1.098x, 1.068x and 1.018x while the 98th percentile moved by 1.008x, 1.009x and 1.001x, so a margin under 1.1 is inside what the stride alone can move and is not judged
what_it_does_not_establish: That the accent is wrong, or that the photograph is right. A reference shot flat or under-saturated lowers the bar it sets, so a pass against a weak photograph means nothing. Three photographs is a small sample and 1.1 is a house number read off it

applies_to: a brand colour whose hue sits in an arc the reference holds at 0.5 percent of the frame or more
threshold: accent chroma / that arc's p98 chroma <= 1.5 passes; above 2.0 fails; between the two is returned for review
formula: 98th percentile chroma of the reference pixels inside the accent's own 30-degree hue arc
verdict_if_failed: fail; CHROMA-INFLATED. The brand version is a saturated swatch that shares only a hue name with the scene
source: This is the arithmetic of the commonest failure in the trade: a palette picked from a list and the photograph dropped in afterwards, so the accent is named after something in the scene rather than measured from it. Print ink is legitimately hotter than glaze under kitchen light, which is why the pass band allows intensification up to 1.5x; both numbers are ours and the band between them is treated as the range over which nobody knows
what_it_does_not_establish: That matching the chroma makes the pair harmonious, or that exceeding it makes them clash. It compares one accent against one photograph and says nothing about lightness, area or what the pair does at their shared edge

applies_to: every non-neutral brand colour proposed against a reference
threshold: the accent's 30-degree hue arc holds at least 0.5 percent of the reference frame
formula: share of sampled pixels with chroma >= 0.04 inside the accent's hue arc
verdict_if_failed: review, never fail; HUE-NOT-IN-REFERENCE. Put the colour in the scene, or declare it as imported contrast
source: A brand hue that appears nowhere in the photograph reads as a rectangle drawn on top, which is the visual signature of a template edit. But a deliberate contrast accent from outside the scene is a legitimate classical device, and one frame is not a brand: a prop, a room, a package or a tradition can carry a colour this photograph never shows. So the gate reports and refuses to judge. The 0.5 percent floor separates a colour the scene contains from compression ringing and chromatic-aberration fringe, and it is ours
what_it_does_not_establish: That the hue belongs to the brand, or that an unanchored hue is a mistake. It also cannot see whether the anchored instance is the subject or a stray object behind it

threshold: every adjacent step within 15 percent of the mean step distance
formula: max(abs(d - mean)) / mean <= tolerance over adjacent OKLab distances
space: OKLab chord distance between adjacent steps
verdict_if_failed: warn; a ramp with an uneven step reads as a missing tone
source: Equal increments of the OKLCH lightness coordinate are not equal perceptual steps once chroma varies, and equal arc length along the path is not equal chord distance between neighbours either, so the ramp is cut by arc length and then relaxed to equalise the chords. Over ten seeds at nine steps this moves the worst step from up to 35.1 percent off the mean to 5.5. The tolerance is ours
what_it_does_not_establish: That the ramp has the right number of steps for the interface, or that its ends are the right ends
